newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blasts hit Telecom, police buildings in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Blasts hit Telecom, police buildings in Corsica.

text.p: Two blasts in the French Mediterranean island of Corsica overnight destroyed a building belonging to state-run France Telecom and another used by paramilitary gendarmerie police, officials said on Wednesday.
Four or five armed and hooded men broke into the telecommunications building in the island capital Ajaccio shortly after midnight (2300 GMT), overpowered the security guard and planted a bomb.
Police said the building was reduced to a pile of rubble and a nearby car was crushed by a flying slab of concrete.
No one has claimed responsibility for the attack, or for the other blast a few hours earlier in Porto-Vecchio in southern Corsica.
A powerful bomb badly damaged a private villa which in the summer serves as lodgings for gendarmerie officers.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, brushing aside Corsican separatist threats, pledged on Tuesday to crack down on the guerrillas' activities but conceded Paris faced a long haul to end bombings.

"I will not let myself be intimidated neither by threats, be they personal, nor by lies," Juppe told the National Assembly in Paris, renewing denials of charges by a separatist leader that the government secretly held abortive peace talks with nationalists earlier this year.

The attacks came days after the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), the island's most hardline separatist group, claimed responsibility for a blast at the home of Emile Zuccarelli, a former cabinet minister and currently mayor of the northern Corsican town of Bastia. He was not at home at the time and no one was hurt.
